title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Tools
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Overview

This handbook page consolidates the most-requested company-wide guidance for new and existing employees at Redwood Inference: how we work, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding timelines, and the primary internal tools used day-to-day. It is intended to be a single source of truth for people-ops, managers, and individual contributors.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & ways of working

Summary
- Mission-driven, engineering-first culture focused on production-grade inference and developer experience.
- Remote-first with optional office hubs in major regions. Team-level policies may set recommended in-office days.
- We expect respectful collaboration, clear async documentation, and measurable outcomes.

Core principles
- Ship with quality: prioritize reliability, observability, and clear rollouts.
- Empathy to customers and teammates: code reviews, RFCs, and thoughtful onboarding.
- Data-driven tradeoffs: use benchmarks, SLOs, and cost metrics to guide decisions.

Working model
- Core hours: 11:00-15:00 local time for meetings (team discretion).
- Flexible hours outside core time; asynchronous communication encouraged.
- Time off: encourage full disconnect during PTO; managers approve based on coverage.

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Overview
- Role families: Engineering, Product, Design, Research/Applied ML, Sales/Go-to-Market, People Ops, Finance/Legal, Customer Success, Security.
- Ladders have three axes: scope, impact, and craft. Promotion decisions consider demonstrated ownership, mentorship, and cross-team outcomes.

Engineering ladder (high-level)
- IC-1 (Associate Engineer): Task execution, learning system design, guided by mentor.
- IC-2 (Engineer): Independent delivery on services/features, reliable code, owns small components.
- IC-3 (Senior Engineer): Designs systems end-to-end, leads medium projects, influences priorities.
- IC-4 (Staff Engineer): Cross-team technical leadership, architecture decisions, performance optimizations.
- IC-5+ (Principal / Distinguished): Long-term technical strategy, platform-level impact.

Manager ladder (high-level)
- Manager I: People manager for small teams (3-5), coaching, performance management.
- Manager II / Director: Manages managers, strategy, cross-functional alignment.

Career development resources
- Quarterly calibration and 1:1s for promotion readiness.
- Learning stipend: $1,000/yr (pro-rated) and conference support for eligible roles.
- Mentorship program: pairing for new hires and promotion candidates.

3) Benefits & Perks (summary)

Compensation & equity
- Competitive base salary with annual review cycle.
- Equity grants for full-time employees; vesting schedules 4 years with 1-year cliff (standard exceptions per offer).

Health & wellbeing
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution.
- Mental health benefits: EAP + therapy stipend.

Time off
- Generous PTO: 25 days of paid time off per year (pro-rated in the first year).
- Additional paid parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (details in parental leave policy).
- Company holidays: observed U.S. federal holidays + 3 floating holidays for regional observance.

Family & lifestyle
- Parental transition coaching, fertility & adoption assistance (covered through benefits vendor).
- Flexible spending (FSA/HSA) where available.

Professional development
- Learning stipend: $1,000 per year, manager approval required.
- Internal conference weeks, tech talks, and knowledge-sharing budgets.

Perks & allowances
- Home office stipend on hire ($500) + annual refresh budget.
- Commuter subsidy in select hub cities.
- Wellness reimbursement ($200/yr).

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Hiring workflow (high-level)
1. Requisition & hiring plan approved by hiring manager + people-ops.
2. Sourcing and screening (recruiter screens then hiring manager screen).
3. Interview loop: technical exercise, system-design (for engineers), pairing session, and final cross-functional interview.
4. Offer, compensation committee sign-off, and background checks as required.

Interview best practices
- Use standardized rubrics tied to role competencies.
- Avoid asking for proprietary coding challenges; provide take-home exercises or live pairing with a shared repo.
- Interview feedback due within 48 hours of loop completion.

New-hire onboarding checklist (first 30 days)
- Pre-start: account provisioning (Okta, GitHub, payroll), equipment ordered.
- Day 1: Welcome meeting, team introductions, security basics, required trainings.
- Week 1: Local onboarding plan, pair with buddy, access to service runbooks and docs.
- Month 1: Deliverable 1 (small project), initial goals set in 1:1 with manager, benefits enrollment complete.

Manager onboarding responsibilities
- Assign buddy and onboarding plan.
- Schedule 30/60/90 check-ins and initial success metrics.
- Ensure access to infra projects, dashboards, and SLO documentation.

5) Internal Tools Guide — quick reference

Account & Access
- Okta: Single Sign-On for most apps. Request app access via Okta Admin or by raising a ticket with IT.
- GitHub: Our org uses teams to manage repo access. Send a request to people-ops for initial repos; engineering leads approve write permissions.

Communication & docs
- Slack: Primary real-time communication. Channels: #all, #eng, #product, and team-specific channels. Use threads and status to keep context.
- Confluence: Source of truth for runbooks, RFCs, and product docs. Use page templates for PRDs and runbooks.

CI/CD & deployments
- CI: GitHub Actions for most services. See CI standards page in eng-infra for job timeouts and secrets handling.
- Deployments: Canary rollouts via Redwood platform; follow rollout checklist in eng-platform/runbooks.

Observability & incident response
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboards per service in eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts.
- PagerDuty: Oncall rotations and escalation policies defined in eng-sre/runbooks.

People Ops & finance
- Payroll/benefits portal: [HR vendor URL] (access via Okta).
- Expenses: Submit via Expensify within 30 days with receipts.

Security & compliance highlight
- MFA required for all accounts.
- Sensitive data: follow data-residency policies and use customer-approved encryption KMS keys for private deployments.

6) Contacts & ownership
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (onboarding, benefits, policy questions)
- IT/Helpdesk: it-support@redwood.com (access, device issues)
- Security: security@redwood.com (incident reporting, exceptions)
- Payroll/Finance: payroll@redwood.com

7) FAQ & common scenarios
- How to request time off: submit PTO via HR portal; managers approve within 5 business days.
- Who signs off on equity grants?: People Ops + compensation committee for non-standard grants.
- How are promotions initiated?: Manager nomination + calibration packet; promotion cycles run quarterly.

Revision history
- 2024-06-01: Created by Maya Rodriguez.

- 2026-01-15: Reviewed and republished; clarified onboarding checklist and added learning stipend details.

Related policies & next steps
- See linked pages for detailed parental leave policy, PTO policy, compensation philosophy, and the engineering career ladder ADRs. Managers should review this page during every new-hire welcome.

Notes
- This document is intended as a living handbook. Submit suggested changes via Confluence inline comments or email people-ops@redwood.com.
